title: Admin Moderation Workflow
purpose: Document the content moderation pipeline from user reporting through auto-flag threshold, admin review, and approve/remove actions
audience: Backend developers, moderators, platform maintainers, QA engineers
description: The content moderation workflow begins when a user (fan) reports content via POST /api/v1/content/:id/report with a reason. The content service creates a report record, then counts all reports for that content. If the count reaches 3 or more, the content status is automatically updated to 'flagged'. The admin opens the moderation panel, which calls GET /api/v1/admin/content/flagged to fetch all flagged content enriched with reportCount and creator info. The admin can then either approve (status → 'published' with auto-dismissal of all reports) or remove (status → 'removed'). Issues: no creator notification when content is flagged or removed, auto-dismiss on approve deletes report audit trail, and no appeal mechanism exists for creators to contest removal.

preconditions: User is authenticated (protect middleware) to submit reports
Content exists and is in active/published state
Admin has valid JWT and admin role for moderation endpoints
Admin is not reporting their own content (no self-report check implemented)
postconditions: Report record created in reports table with pending status
If report count >= 3: content status changed to 'flagged' — enters moderation queue
Admin can view all flagged content enriched with report count and creator info
Approve: content restored to 'published'; all pending reports dismissed
Remove: content status changed to 'removed'; creator not notified

decisions.truePath: Update content status to 'flagged' — enters moderation queue
decisions.falsePath: No action on content status — report recorded only

decisions.condition: Does admin approve or remove the content?
decisions.truePath: Approve: restore to published, dismiss all reports. Remove: set status to removed.
decisions.falsePath: Admin can also take no action, leaving content flagged.

errorPaths.trigger: No creator notification on flag or remove
errorPaths.destination: Creator unaware their content was flagged or removed
errorPaths.recovery: Feature gap — creator discovers via next page load or user complaints

errorPaths.destination: Removed content has no appeal process

validationRules: User must be authenticated (protect) to report content
Admin must have protectAndAdmin for all moderation endpoints
Report reason must be non-empty string
Content must exist (404 if not found)
Approve/remove endpoints require contentId in URL params
businessRules: Auto-flag threshold: 3 reports trigger content status change to 'flagged'
Reports are counted cumulatively — all reports for the content, not just since last action
Approving content auto-dismisses ALL pending reports (delete, not status change)
No notification sent to creator when content is flagged or removed
No appeal mechanism exists for creators to contest removal
No distinction between report types — all reports weighted equally
securityConsiderations: Users can report content without restriction (potential abuse through mass false reporting)
Auto-flag at 3 reports is a low threshold — coordinated bad actors can easily trigger flags
No self-report guard — creator could report own content to trigger unnecessary moderation
No admin audit trail — admin actions not logged
Removal is permanent — no undo or appeal mechanism
performanceConsiderations: Report count query runs on every report submission — additional DB call
Flagged content enrichment iterates each item for report fetch and creator lookup
No pagination on flagged content endpoint — could return many items
Auto-flag is inline operation — adds latency to report endpoint

annotations.label: 🟡 No Creator Notification
annotations.description: Creator is not notified when their content is flagged or removed. No email, no in-app notification.

annotations.label: 🟡 Auto-Dismiss on Approve Destroys Audit Trail
annotations.description: All reports are deleted when content is approved. No history of past reports remains.

annotations.label: 🔴 No Appeal Mechanism
annotations.description: Creator cannot appeal a removal decision. Removed content stays removed permanently.

annotations.label: Low auto-flag threshold
annotations.description: 3 reports trigger auto-flag. Coordinated bad actors can easily trigger false flags.
